defects.defect: The same observation serves both sides. 'R-89 not adopted, but work ran under it' is read as H-D's status clause failing. But the spec's own P2 and P7 falsifiers read the same observation as non-conformance: execution under an act that is not in force, before WP-4B's acceptance and with no waiver. That falsifies H-B. H-D can say 'R-89 had no force; engineering broke the norm'. H-B can say 'work changed the norm'. Behavioural uptake cannot tell the norm changed without an act from work violated an unchanged norm. The same confound affects P5's 'not in force' branch and P1's H-D falsifier, which requires only that the after-state is 'acted on by engineering'.
defects.correction: Record the six distinctions separately (spec.shared_rules.six_distinctions). Define independent observables of the norm in force: NIF-A (an independent norm-status record), NIF-B (application of the norm as binding by an actor who is neither the maker/adopter nor the executor), and NIF-C (citation by such an actor, which is recorded only). Executor work is never NIF; it is recorded as ACT-CONF or ACT-CONTRA. Add rule G-D1: a premise about force that is established only by executor behaviour, or by applying H-D's status rule to the maker's records, grades any falsifier as DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, H-B clause}. Give each prediction a NIF requirement (spec.nif_matrix), or declare it NON-DISCRIMINATING or DISJUNCTIVE without one. Split the headline test into an H-D force limb (NIF-A or NIF-B, with no adoption form) and an H-B conformance limb (an execution trace, plus non-permission at t- by NIF or the graded fallback). This narrows the reviewer's fix: bare third-party citation only establishes that the norm is known to be in force, so it cannot fire a falsifier.
defects.sufficiency: D1 is an identification failure: observation O is predicted both by (H-D status holds and H-B conformance fails) and by (H-D status fails and H-B conformance holds). After the correction, the two limbs use disjoint observables. The H-D limb uses NIF-A or NIF-B, which are not executor acts, so H-B's conformance clause is silent about them. The H-B limb uses non-permission established without H-D's status rule, because G-D1 downgrades any premise that uses it. Executor behaviour enters only as ACT-CONF or ACT-CONTRA, never as N-FORCE or N-CHANGE-NOACT, so no single observation can count for both sides. When only O is present, DISJUNCTIVE is the strongest conclusion that logically follows.
defects.prediction_change: Yes, operationally; the hypothesis-level claims are unchanged. The P4-HD falsifier now needs NIF-A or NIF-B, and work citing R-89 no longer suffices. The P1-HD after-state needs NIF, and engineering uptake no longer suffices. Both P5 branches need NIF, or the result is DISJUNCTIVE. The P2 and P7 H-B falsifiers become DISJUNCTIVE when non-permission rests on the status rule. The first 1bb section-5 branch becomes DISJUNCTIVE unless NIF is present.
defects.frozen_rule: FR-D1: Executor behaviour establishes at most ACT-CONF or ACT-CONTRA, never N-FORCE or N-CHANGE-NOACT. A premise 'N (not) in force at t' counts toward a falsifier only via NIF-A or NIF-B; NIF-C, maker statements, ruling self-assertions and recording times never count. G-D1: a premise established only by executor behaviour, or by applying H-D's status rule to the maker's records, makes the falsifier DISJUNCTIVE {H-D clause, H-B clause}. Each prediction carries the NIF requirement in spec.nif_matrix; without it, it is scored as that table's 'without' column.

defects.defect: Not well defined. (a) R-86 names the adopter; the single channel is the spec's own assumption. The Chief's operational dispositions (R-94, and R-90's operational/constitutional split) and the DA's 'R-89 already governs' may sit in other channels, such as session logs or progress files. An act made there would show up as an 'act-less change'. (b) Late recording: an act decided in the window but recorded afterwards looks like 'no entry in window'. The spec has no rule for this, although recording != decision is a SOURCE FACT. (c) There is no rule, fixed in advance, for what form counts as an adoption. The spec says the DA's statement 'may itself be the adoption' and leaves it there, so the outcome can be decided after the fact. (d) Actor identity rests on git author/committer names, which the actor sets. (e) There is no closed world for work, yet P1-HB ('executed nothing'), P7 ('first work event') and the status-mediation contrast ('no execution') all need an absence of work. (f) 'Fixed before looking at the data' is impossible: R-86 and R-90 have already been read.
defects.correction: (a) A declared channel set DCS v0 = {K-REG, K-SESS, K-PROG}, extended by Part C and closed as DCS v1 before Stage 1. A find outside it is labelled OUT_OF_CHANNEL_ACT, which makes the premise UNDETERMINED. (b) An act recorded after window W that claims an effect inside W makes both 'no act' and 'act in force' NOT_IDENTIFIABLE. (c) The adoption forms AF-1, AF-2 and AF-3 are exhaustive. Descriptive force assertions by the maker ('already governs') are MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION, not adoption; a sensitivity result is reported but never scored. (d) AUTH_ID (a verified signature or a hosting-server account record) versus ACTOR_SET_ID; ACTOR_SET_ID caps the grade at FIRED-CONDITIONAL. (e) An execution-channel register EC; an absence of work needs a complete EC. (f) Rules are fixed before acquisition, not before reading; the non-blindness toward R-86 and R-90 is disclosed; operational capability is UNKNOWN.
defects.sufficiency: Each sub-defect is a path by which a 'no act' or 'no work' premise could come out true when an act or work in fact existed, or be decided after the fact. Each fix blocks that path: an out-of-channel act blocks the premise; late recording makes it NOT_IDENTIFIABLE; the adoption verdict is fixed by a prior rule; identities set by actors cannot support a clean grade; an absence of work needs completeness; and the freeze is verifiable because it precedes acquisition. No falsifier is removed; only its missing premises are added.

defects.defect: The attestation rule contradicts itself. Condition (i) requires an author or process different from the norm-making record, but entry into force is taken from the adoption record written by the adopter, which is the status-conferring act. Condition (ii) excludes artefacts that are 'citing that record', but P4 needs uptake artefacts that cite R-89.
defects.correction: Separate being the observation from attesting a field of it. An act's own record is the observation of the act. It attests only its writer (AUTH_ID or ACTOR_SET_ID) and its recording time, never its stated effective date or the norm's force. Conditions (i)-(iii) apply only to attesting fields of other observations. Citing artefacts are admissible as observations of uptake (NIF-B, NIF-C, ACT); only copying self-statements to attest a field is excluded.
defects.sufficiency: Both contradictions came from applying one rule to two roles. With the roles separated, the adoption record and the uptake artefacts each satisfy the rule in the role they play. No field is attested by self-report, because effective dates and force are never self-attested.
defects.prediction_change: No. It narrows what an adoption record can establish (never the effective date), which matters for the time premises of P4 and P7.
defects.frozen_rule: FR-D7: A record of an act attests only (i) its writer (AUTH_ID or ACTOR_SET_ID) and (ii) its recording time. A field of any other observation is independently attested only if the attesting artefact (i) has a writer that is not the maker, adopter or executor, (ii) does not copy the ruling's self-statements, and (iii) carries a system-generated time. Citing artefacts are admissible as observations of uptake.

N-EXISTS.meaning: the norm exists (a text is recorded, PREPARED included)
N-EXISTS.established_by: the record's text; its time is a recording time

N-FORCE.meaning: the norm is in force at t
N-FORCE.established_by: NIF-A, or NIF-B (N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL]); the graded fallback gives at most FIRED-CONDITIONAL
N-FORCE.never_by: self-assertion, maker statements, recording time, executor behaviour, N-EXISTS alone

N-KNOWN.meaning: the norm is known or claimed to be in force by actor X
N-KNOWN.established_by: X's statement: NIF-C (third party), MAKER_FORCE_ASSERTION (maker), SELF_ASSERTION (in the ruling)

ACT-CONF.meaning: an act according to a norm: an execution at t permitted by the norms in force at t-
ACT-CONF.established_by: an execution trace plus N-FORCE of a permitting norm at t-

ACT-CONTRA.meaning: an act contrary to a norm: an execution at t not permitted at t-
ACT-CONTRA.established_by: an execution trace plus N-FORCE of a prohibition at t-, or the absence of any permitting norm in force at t- (needs a complete DCS)

N-CHANGE-NOACT.meaning: a norm changes without a norm-making act
N-CHANGE-NOACT.established_by: N-FORCE at t1 != N-FORCE at t2 (both by NIF); a complete DCS with no act in [t1,t2], no prior conditional act, and no late-recorded act claiming effect in [t1,t2]
N-CHANGE-NOACT.never_by: a work event alone; a ruling asserting its own adoption

nif.NIF-A: An entry in a channel meeting I1-I4 (scoping_protocol.criteria) that records the normative state at t with a system time. Its availability comes from Part C.
nif.NIF-B: An act by an actor who is not the maker/adopter of the norm and not the executor of the work under test, applying the norm as binding (grant, refuse, accept, block), with AUTH_ID and a recording time. It establishes N-FORCE[OPERATIONAL] (PROPOSAL). If later expressly voided as erroneous, it is downgraded to FIRED-CONDITIONAL.
nif.NIF-C: A citation by such an actor, without application. It establishes N-KNOWN only, and never fires a falsifier.

timestamp_rules: The earliest trace = the ancestry-minimal ET set; its times are reported as %aI and %cI, both SOURCE_STATED.
CLOCK_ANOMALY: for an ancestry pair a < b with cI(b) < cI(a), date-based order involving them is NOT_IDENTIFIABLE.
Order vs the decision or entry into force of any norm is always NOT_IDENTIFIABLE from this channel.

absence.definition: Positive control non-empty; capture valid; zero ET-1 and ET-2 among PRIMARY hits.
absence.label: NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE
why: --all sees only this clone's refs: deleted or force-pushed branches, unfetched refs and other repositories are invisible
the search is identifier-based: unlabelled work is invisible; sensitivity beyond the positive control is unknown
work may exist outside git (CI-only, uncommitted, other systems)
the clone may be shallow or partial
completeness_required_for_ABSENT_IN_COMP: C1: not shallow, no partial-clone filter (checked here)
C2: every ls-remote object present locally (checked here)
C3: server-side evidence of no ref deletion or force-push over the window (Part C, K-HOST-AUDIT)

C4: an execution-channel rule, recorded in a channel independent of the executor, making REPO the sole channel for WP-4C-1 work and requiring the identifier in messages, with enforcement records (Part C)
absence.CAPTURE_INVALID: Positive control empty, or C1 or C2 fails. This is not an absence.

window.reason: FR-D4: work before R-89's recording, or before R-72, is the strongest case against H-B. --since/--until filter on actor-set committer dates, and --since can stop the traversal early on clock skew.
window.upper_bound: the ref snapshot at capture (01_refs.tsv), recorded and hashed
window.post_hoc_tags: Descriptive only, by both SOURCE_STATED dates: PRE_R72_DATE (< 2026-08-02), CORPUS_SPAN (2026-08-02..2026-08-15), POST_CORPUS (> 2026-08-15). The P7 window is applied in Stage 1, not in the search.

commands.prerequisites: git >= 2.31, bash, GNU coreutils; record git --version
rank0-fetch.sh: # rank0-fetch.sh -- frozen by SPEC-r1 Part B. Do not edit. Run from the root of the worker's clone of REPO.
PRE="${PRE:?set PRE to a new empty directory}"
for r in $(git remote); do git ls-remote --refs "$r" | sed "s|^|$r |"; done | sort > "$PRE/07_ls_remote.txt"
awk '{print $2}' "$PRE/07_ls_remote.txt" | sort -u | while read -r s; do if git cat-file -e "$s" 2>/dev/null; then echo "present $s"; else echo "MISSING $s"; fi; done > "$PRE/08_remote_objects.txt"
( cd "$PRE" && find . -type f | sort | xargs -r sha256sum ) > "$PRE.SHA256SUMS"
rank0-wp4c1.sh: # rank0-wp4c1.sh -- frozen by SPEC-r1 Part B. Do not edit. Run from the root of a clone of REPO.
export LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC GIT_PAGER=cat GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1
OUT="${OUT:?set OUT to a new empty directory}"
g() { git --no-replace-objects -c core.quotepath=off -c log.showSignature=false -c log.mailmap=false -c diff.renames=false -c color.ui=never "$@"; }

{ git --version; g rev-parse --show-toplevel; g rev-parse --is-shallow-repository; g config --get extensions.partialClone || echo 'partialClone=unset'; g config --get remote.origin.promisor || echo 'promisor=unset'; } > "$OUT/00_env.txt"
# S3 variant passes (reported separately; never counted as primary)
{ g fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs --no-progress 2>/dev/null || true; } | { grep -E '^unreachable commit ' || true; } | cut -d' ' -f3 | sort > "$OUT/32_unreachable.txt"

if [ -s "$OUT/32_unreachable.txt" ]; then g log --no-walk --stdin -E --grep="$PAT" --format="$FMT" < "$OUT/32_unreachable.txt" > "$OUT/33_unreachable_msg.tsv"; else : > "$OUT/33_unreachable_msg.tsv"; fi
# S5 anchors: recording of ruling ids in REPO (never evidence of decision or force)
for id in R72 R87 R89; do
# S6 hit set, details, matching lines, signatures, ancestry
while read -r h; do echo "== $h"; g show --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --format=fuller --name-status "$h"; done < "$OUT/90_hitset.txt" > "$OUT/93_details.txt"

while read -r h; do echo "== $h"; g show --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --format= -U0 "$h" | awk -v pat="$PAT" '/^[+][+][+] /{f=$2} /^[+-]/ && !/^([+][+][+]|---) / && $0 ~ pat {print f " " $0}'; done < "$OUT/90_hitset.txt" > "$OUT/94_matching_lines.txt"
while read -r h; do echo "$h $(g cat-file commit "$h" | grep -c '^gpgsig' || true)"; done < "$OUT/90_hitset.txt" > "$OUT/92_sig_presence.txt"

while read -r a; do while read -r b; do if [ "$a" != "$b" ] && g merge-base --is-ancestor "$a" "$b"; then echo "$a $b" >> "$OUT/95_ancestry.txt"; fi; done < "$OUT/95a_nodes.txt"; done < "$OUT/95a_nodes.txt"
awk 'NR==FNR{h[$1]=1; next} ($1 in h) && ($2 in h){print $2}' "$OUT/90_hitset.txt" "$OUT/95_ancestry.txt" | sort -u > "$OUT/96_hits_with_hit_ancestor.txt"
( cd "$OUT" && find . -type f | sort | xargs -r sha256sum ) > "$OUT.SHA256SUMS"
rank0-order.sh: # rank0-order.sh -- frozen by SPEC-r1 Part B. Do not edit.
awk 'NR==FNR{h[$1]=1; next} ($1 in h) && ($2 in h){print $2}' "$ET" "$OUT/95_ancestry.txt" | sort -u > "$OUT/99a_et_with_et_ancestor.txt"
while read -r h; do git --no-replace-objects log -1 --format='%H%x09%aI%x09%cI' "$h"; done < "$OUT/99b_et_ancestry_minimal.txt" > "$OUT/99c_et_minimal_dates.tsv"
commands.hashing: Every output file is hashed with SHA-256 into SHA256SUMS (and 99_SHA256SUMS); the SHA-256 of SHA256SUMS goes into the report. 98_canonical_key = SHA-256(refs snapshot || sorted hit set); it is independent of the git version, and runs on the same refs must match. repo.bundle is hashed in PRE/SHA256SUMS.

procedure.freeze: The human names REPO. The reviewer extracts the three scripts verbatim from SPEC-r1.md and records their SHA-256 in FREEZE.txt. No rule changes after this point; a change means protocol r2, refrozen before any rerun.
worker: W1 verify script hashes vs FREEZE.txt; stop on mismatch
W2 run rank0-fetch.sh in the working clone (PRE)
W3 Run A: rank0-wp4c1.sh in the working clone (OUT_A), including LOCAL_ONLY channels
W4 Run B: git clone --mirror PRE/repo.bundle rb; run rank0-wp4c1.sh there (OUT_B). PRIMARY results come from Run B; Run A's primary hit set must be a superset of Run B's; extras are LOCAL_ONLY
W5 on any command error: stop, keep stderr, report CAPTURE_ERROR; no ad-hoc fixes
W6 validity: 05_control non-empty; not shallow, no partial clone (C1); no MISSING in 08 (C2); else CAPTURE_INVALID
W7 classify every hit in 90_hitset per execution_trace; write CLASSIFICATION.tsv (hash, class, flags, rule clause, path classes, %aI, %cI, date tag, signature presence)
W8 write the ET list; run rank0-order.sh; assign order labels

W9 write RANK0-REPORT.md: labels, SHA-256 of each SHA256SUMS, canonical key, variant and LOCAL_ONLY counts, date tags; no statement about the hypotheses (the O0-O8 mapping is a separate step after acceptance)
reviewer: independent: no shared session; does not see the worker's classification before R3
R1 verify the script hashes, all SHA256SUMS and the bundle hash
R2 mirror-clone the same bundle, rerun rank0-wp4c1.sh; byte-identical with the same git version, otherwise the same 98_canonical_key
R3 classify blind, then compare; resolve only by quoting the rule clause; unresolved cases = DISPUTED, passed to the human; never silently choose the worse class
R4 check the positive control, C1/C2, that variants are not counted, and that the absence wording is exactly NOT-EVIDENCED-IN-CAPTURE unless C3 and C4 are shown
R5 check that nothing goes beyond the labels and no git time is presented as a decision time or entry into force
procedure.constraint: Neither role widens the search; new ideas are written down as proposals for protocol r2.

output_labels.earliest_trace: The ancestry-minimal ET set (99b), with SOURCE_STATED %aI and %cI.

order.SOURCE_STATED_ORDER: no ancestry; author-date and committer-date orders agree; no CLOCK_ANOMALY. Also textual orders ('after R-87', cherry-pick trailers)
order.INFERRED_ORDER: only via a chain combining RECORDING and SOURCE_STATED links, written out
order.NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: otherwise; dates disagree; CLOCK_ANOMALY; the other event is outside git

output_labels.always_not_identifiable: The order of any WP-4C-1 trace vs the decision or entry into force of R-72, R-87, R-89 or WP-4B's acceptance. Anchor commits show only when text containing those ids was recorded in REPO.

scoping_protocol.question: Does an independent record of the norm in force exist, maintained by someone other than the norm-maker, the executor or the self-asserting ruling? Answer only Q1-Q8. No general archaeology.

scope-nsc.sh: # scope-nsc.sh -- frozen by SPEC-r1 Part C. Existence/metadata only. Do not edit. Run from REPO root.
OUT="${OUT:?set OUT to a new empty directory}"
DEF="$(g symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null || g rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
while read -r p; do echo "== $p"; g show "$DEF:$p"; done < "$OUT/53_K-CFG_paths.txt" > "$OUT/56_codeowners_content.txt"
{ g config --get core.hooksPath || echo 'hooksPath=unset'; ls -1 .git/hooks 2>/dev/null | { grep -v '[.]sample$' || true; }; } > "$OUT/57_local_hooks_LOCAL_ONLY.txt"

while read -r p; do echo "== $p"; g log --all --diff-filter=A --format='%H%x09%aI%x09%cI' -- "$p" | tail -n 1; g log --all --format='%an%x09%ae' -- "$p" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn; done < "$OUT/$f"_paths.txt
g log --all --format='%H' | while read -r h; do if g cat-file commit "$h" | grep -q '^gpgsig'; then echo S; else echo U; fi; done | sort | uniq -c > "$OUT/59a_commit_sig_counts.txt"
g for-each-ref refs/tags --format='%(objecttype) %(refname)' | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c > "$OUT/59b_tag_types.txt"
if grep -qi 'gitlab' "$OUT/59d_remotes.txt"; then HOST=gitlab; elif grep -qi 'github[.]com' "$OUT/59d_remotes.txt"; then HOST=github; fi
if [ "$HOST" = gitlab ]; then cmd=(glab api "$2"); else cmd=(gh api "$2"); fi

if "${cmd[@]}" > "$OUT/tmp.json" 2> "$OUT/62_$1.err"; then jq -S "$3" "$OUT/tmp.json" > "$OUT/62_$1.json"; echo "$1 OK" >> "$OUT/61_api_status.txt"; else echo "$1 FAIL $(head -c 200 "$OUT/62_$1.err" | tr '\n' ' ')" >> "$OUT/61_api_status.txt"; fi
api project 'projects/:id' '{id, path_with_namespace, default_branch, created_at, merge_requests_enabled, only_allow_merge_if_pipeline_succeeds, merge_method}'

api protected_branches 'projects/:id/protected_branches' '[.[] | {name, allow_force_push, code_owner_approval_required, push: [.push_access_levels[]?.access_level_description], merge: [.merge_access_levels[]?.access_level_description]}]'
api member_roles 'projects/:id/members/all?per_page=100' '[.[] | .access_level] | group_by(.) | map({level: .[0], n: length})'
api repo 'repos/{owner}/{repo}' '{full_name, default_branch, created_at, allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge, allow_rebase_merge}'

api branch_protection "repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/${DEF#origin/}/protection" '{required_signatures: .required_signatures.enabled, enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, reviews: .required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, codeowners: .required_pull_request_reviews.require_code_owner_reviews, allow_force_pushes: .allow_force_pushes.enabled}'
api collaborator_roles 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators?per_page=100' '[.[] | .role_name] | group_by(.) | map({role: .[0], n: length})'
( cd "$OUT" && find . -type f | sort | xargs -r sha256sum ) > "$OUT.SHA256SUMS"
notes: HOST = none: all K-HOST-* channels = SERVER_CHANNELS_UNCHECKED, Q1 = UNKNOWN
an API FAIL with 401/403/404 = NOT_ACCESSIBLE, never NO
API projections are hashed; their reproducibility is LIMITED (server data change)

independence.I1: writer: entries written by a process or actor that is not the maker/adopter (DA, Chief), not the executor (engineering), and not the ruling (e.g. hosting server, CI system, independent secretariat)
independence.I2: derivation: entries are not copies or summaries of the rulings' self-statements
independence.I3: clock: timestamps generated by the channel's system, not by the writer's client
independence.I4: integrity: maker and executor cannot silently alter or delete entries (append-only, or audited changes)
independence.grades: INDEPENDENT = I1-I4 all hold; PARTIAL(list) = at least one holds; NOT_INDEPENDENT = none holds
independence.note: A channel that records a maker's act (e.g. an MR approval by the DA) can be PARTIAL (I3 and I4 for time and identity), but it is not an independent record of the norm in force (FR-D13).

completeness.K1: coverage: the event type is required to pass through the channel (e.g. a protected branch with no direct push; a mandatory MR)
completeness.K2: retention: records exist from before the window start (before-window queries are non-empty)
completeness.K3: config stability: coverage configuration unchanged over the window (needs the audit log; the current configuration does not show the configuration then in force, per M-TIME)
completeness.K4: integrity: I4, or the audit log shows no deletions
completeness.grades: COMPLETE_SHOWN = K1-K4 all hold; PARTIAL(list); UNKNOWN

questions.derived_from: the channel type, not its content (K-STATUS = UNKNOWN_CONTENT)
member roles, protected-branch levels, CODEOWNERS, path-history author metadata (ACTOR_SET_ID; indicative only)
channel type (git = CLIENT_SET; server API = SYSTEM_GENERATED)

questions.text: Can it establish the norm in force at time t?
questions.derived_from: YES iff it records NORM_STATE with I3 and K2 covers t; PARTIAL iff only ADOPTION_EVENT or APPROVAL_EVENT times; else NO

questions.text: Can it be reproduced and verified?
questions.derived_from: content-addressed, or re-queryable with the stated access = YES; access-restricted, mutable or retention-limited = LIMITED

scoping_protocol.overall_result: NIF_A_CHANNEL_EXISTS iff some channel has Q1 = YES, Q5 = YES, Q7 = INDEPENDENT and Q6 != UNKNOWN; otherwise NO_NIF_A_CHANNEL_IN_CHECKED_SET (noting SERVER_CHANNELS_UNCHECKED where it applies).
consequences: If NO_NIF_A_CHANNEL_IN_CHECKED_SET: predictions whose nif_matrix requirement accepts only NIF-A fall to 'without'; those accepting NIF-B stay open until Stage 1
DCS v1 += every channel with Q2 containing ADOPTION_EVENT or APPROVAL_EVENT
EC += CI run history if Q1 = YES
Part B C3 is satisfied only by K-HOST-AUDIT; C4 only by K-HOOK or K-HOST-CFG with a commit-message rule plus K3
scoping_protocol.procedure: As in Part B: the script hash is frozen in FREEZE.txt; one run; the reviewer checks that every answer cell cites its output file, that no prohibited content was read, reruns the git part (files 50-59) and compares hashes; the API part is compared by status and projection shape.
scoping_protocol.output: SCOPING-REPORT.md: one row per K-* channel answering Q1-Q8; the overall result; the resulting DCS v1 and EC; the SHA-256 of SHA256SUMS.
